newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to transfer Palestinians 1.2 bln shekels.
newsitem.headline: Israel to transfer Palestinians 1.2 bln shekels.

text.p: Israel will transfer 1.2 billion shekels to the Palestinian Authority this year as part of the VAT and customs restitutions defined by the 1994 economic agreement, a senior Treasury official said on Wednesday.

Aryeh Zaeff, head of customs and value added tax (VAT) at the Finance Ministry, said that payments include VAT restitutions, restitutions on taxes paid on gasoline bought in Israel and customs and taxes levied on imports meant for the Palestinian Authority.
In 1995 Israel transferred about 800 million shekels to the Authority, he said.

The payments do not include purchase taxes paid on goods bought in Israel. The Palestinians have requested the transfer of these taxes as well and Zaeff recently said the Finance Ministry was considering the request. Purchase taxes are levied on most goods including imports.

Israel's monthly transfers to the Palestinian Authority total 90 million to 100 million shekels. But Zaeff said this figure could be lower in the coming months as Palestinians may start buying less from Israel because of recent political unrest.
The United States is hosting an emergency Middle East summit in Washington in an attempt to get peace talks back on track following clashes between Palestinians and Israeli soldiers.
Zaeff said that in 1995 Palestinians bought an estimated $1.8 billion in goods and services from Israel.
